The existing app is a mobile-first 2D game. The user wants a 3D FPS like Counter-Strike with knives, weapons and skins, crates, cases. I will rewrite this into a 3D FPS using Three.js. Need vendored three.js.

Let me plan the game:

**Arsenal Strike** (name maybe "DUSTLINE: ARSENAL" or new brand "BLACKSITE"). Let's call it "ASHFALL" or keep DUSTLINE? Better a new identity: "STRIKE//LINE"? Let's do "DUSTLINE: ARMS DEAL" — hmm. The request is CS-like. I'll build **"BLACKSITE // ARMS"**... Let's keep DUSTLINE branding but add "ARSENAL". Actually the menu visuals are nice and thematic. I'll rebrand to **"IRONLINE"**? I'd rather create "DUSTLINE" continuing brand: "DUSTLINE: ARSENAL — OFFLINE TACTICAL FPS".

Features needed:
- First person 3D with mouse look, pointer lock, WASD movement, sprint, crouch, jump maybe.
- Weapons: knife, pistol, SMG, rifle, AWP-like sniper, shotgun? With viewmodels (low-poly procedural gun models built with three.js boxes), recoil, muzzle flash, tracers, hitscan raycasting, headshot multiplier.
- Skins: weapon skins with rarity (Factory New etc.), patterns/colors applied to materials, inspect animation.
- Crates/cases: case opening UI with scrolling reel animation, rarity colors, drop rates, keys/case currency earned by kills.
- Bots: enemy models with simple AI, health bars, death animations.
- Map: a dust2-ish environment: crates, containers, walls, bombsite, skybox, lighting.
- Buy phase? Maybe simpler: armory screen where you equip skins, and loadout selection before match.
- HUD: health, armor, ammo, crosshair, kill feed, round timer, score, radar/minimap.
- Sound via WebAudio (procedural gunshots, reload, hit marker, case opening). That improves feel a lot with no assets.
- Round-based: first to 5 rounds, T vs CT? Keep team deathmatch-ish rounds with bots. Simpler: deathmatch against bots; score. But CS-like: rounds. Let's do round-based elimination: you + 2 teammates vs 3 enemies, first to 4. That we can do.

Scope: significant but doable in a few files. Let's structure:

- index.html — game shell + screens (menu, armory, case opening overlay, HUD, pause, round end).
- styles.css — rewrite fully for the new UI.
- src/ ... but no build step; use ES modules. Vendored three: `vendor/three.module.js`. Then game.js as ES module importing three.

Check if three module has other imports? three.module.js is self-contained. Good. Use r160 or newer. Download from jsdelivr.

Also need an environment texture? Use procedural sky (gradient), fog, hemisphere light, directional light with shadows (shadow map moderate). Textures procedural via canvas for crates/ground/walls. Keep perf decent with SwiftShader.

Rendering details for a good look:
- Ground: large plane with canvas-generated sand/dust texture repeating, some debris decals.
- Walls: boxes with canvas concrete texture.
- Sky: big sphere with gradient shader, sun disk? Use scene.background = gradient texture from canvas, plus fog color.
- Lighting: hemisphere + directional with shadow, ACES tone mapping, sRGB.
- Post-processing? Avoid for perf. Use tone mapping and fog; add vignette CSS overlay.
- Viewmodel: group attached to camera, procedural weapons from boxes; render with separate camera? Simpler: attach to camera, but clipping into walls. Use a second scene/camera overlay for weapon viewmodel to avoid clipping and get consistent lighting: render main scene, then clear depth and render weapon scene with same camera? Use two cameras: main camera fov 75, weapon camera fov 55 positioned same, weapon group at fixed offset. Common technique: `renderer.autoClear=false; render(main); renderer.clearDepth(); render(weaponScene, weaponCamera)`. Weapon camera copies rotation from main camera. Good.

Procedural viewmodels: define gun builder functions using BoxGeometry/CylinderGeometry with materials. Make it look decent: stock, receiver, barrel, mag, grip, scope, suppressor etc. Materials: metal dark, tan, plus skin material with color/camo pattern generated texture.

Knife model: blade (extruded shape or box tapered), handle. Knife attack: slash animation with camera sway, raycast short range, instakill from behind maybe (backstab 2x).

Skins: Each weapon has skin definitions with names, rarity tiers, color palettes and pattern types (solid, camo, fade, stripes, hex). Generate CanvasTexture for the skin pattern applied to main body. Cases contain skins. Rarity colors: Consumer #b0c3d9, Industrial #5e98d9, Mil-Spec #4b69ff, Restricted #8847ff, Classified #d32ce6, Covert #eb4b4b, Knife ★ #ffd700 (gold).

Case system:
- Earn credits from kills (e.g., $100 per kill, round win $300). Or use credits as currency, and crates drop randomly after matches? Simpler: earn "credits" (in-game) — buy cases for 100 credits, keys are free (avoid key paywall). Case opening animation: horizontal reel of items scrolling with cubic easing to land on selected item. Determine item by weighted random, build 40 filler items, place the winner at index 34, animate. Reveal card with rarity flourish.
- Cases: "Field Case" (basic), "Operator Case", "Elite Case" with different pools, including knives.
- Inventory: skins listed, equip per weapon slot. Each skin tied to a weapon. Equipping changes viewmodel skin. Save inventory in localStorage. Reset option.
- Every kill gives credits; also "crate drop" chance after round win giving a free case.

Armory UI: tabs: LOADOUT (weapon slots: primary/secondary/knife, equip skins), CASES (open), INVENTORY (all skins). Given complexity, keep tabs: LOADOUT / CASES / INVENTORY maybe combine loadout+inventory: list owned skins grouped by weapon, click to equip; a "cases" tab.

Default loadout: pistol (P2000-ish "P9 SIDEARM"), rifle "V-9 STRIKER" (AK-like), knife "TAC KNIFE". Maybe allow choosing primary among 3 (assault, SMG, sniper) unlocked by default to make game fun. Keep loadout: primary slot with 3 weapon options; secondary 2 options; knife.

Gameplay structure:
- Menu → play → choose loadout via armory (persistent) → DEPLOY.
- Pointer lock on click. ESC pauses via pointerlockchange.
- Round timer 2:00; first team to 4 rounds. Bots with pathing around obstacles using simple steering + line of sight. Keep bot count 3v3 with player.
- Bomb? No, keep elimination. Objective: eliminate enemy squad both sides. CS-like defuse would be much extra. Add a "hostage"? Skip. Elimination + timer.
- Weapon switching with 1/2/3. Reload R. B (buy) not needed.
- Damage: hitscan raycast against bot hitboxes (head sphere + body capsule). Headshot damage x4. Armor reduces.
- Bot AI: navigate toward player using simple obstacle avoidance; shoot with inaccuracy increasing with distance, telegraphed muzzle flash. Add hit reaction, death ragdoll-lite (fall over rotation).
- Hit registration: use Raycaster against bot meshes with userData.bot; separate head mesh.
- Tracer: line/beam quickly fading from muzzle to hit point; impact sparks (small particles), decals (sprite planes) optional.
- Muzzle flash light + sprite.
- Screen shake, recoil (pitch/yaw), spread bloom, ADS for sniper (right mouse scope overlay). Nice to have: right click to aim down sights for sniper with scope overlay.
- Sounds: WebAudio synthesized: gunshot noise burst + low thump, reload clicks, knife whoosh, hit marker tick, headshot ding, case open whoosh, rare drop shimmer, footsteps. Implement an audio module with noise buffer.

Performance: shadow map 1024 with directional light and limited casters. Many objects; fine.

Mini-map radar: canvas 2D overlay drawing map obstacles and dots.

I'll add basic touch controls (left stick move, right area look, fire button, reload, weapon buttons) so it's playable on mobile too. But keep it simpler: touch look drag + joystick + fire. Worth adding but don't overinvest.
